title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. This is the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' sequel to La Longue Marche (1981). Grothendieck is analysing a Teichmüller–Galois type group SΓ^! of triples u=(u,a,b). Here u is a profinite element and a, b live in profinite completions attached to the elliptic generators ρ (ρ^3 = −1) and σ (σ^2 = −1). The setting is SL_2/PSL_2-like: the next page has μ ↪ L_ρ×L_σ, −1 ↦ (ρ^3, σ^2). The group carries two sign characters ε_2, ε_3 with values in μ = {±1}. Superscripts Π and Π_0 denote congruence conditions u ≡ b, u ≡ ε_3[σ]a, taken modulo Π̂ or Π̂_0. The group Ŝ_0^Π Γ^! is an extension of Z^! ≅ M[0], a genus-0 modular-type group, by μ.

Step 1. Equation (82), written as a sequence on the previous page, is 1→μ→Ŝ_0^{Π}Γ^{!0}→Ŝ_0Γ^{!0}→1. The page notes that this sequence is split by Ŝ_0^{Π_0}Γ^{!0}, so Ŝ_0^Π Γ^{!0} = Ŝ_0^{Π_0}Γ^{!0} × μ. (The bottom group in the transcribed sequence should read Ŝ_0Γ^{!0}; on the previous page it was transcribed as S_0Γ^{!0}.)

Step 2. The preceding conjugation computations, eqs. (76)–(80), show that Ŝ_0^{Π_0}Γ^{!'} and Ŝ_0^{Π_0}Γ^{!'''} are not normal. The page adds that Ŝ_0^{Π_0}Γ^{!0}, of index 8 in Ŝ_0^Π Γ^!, is normal.

Step 3 (Proposition). Take the canonical set-theoretic section A of Ŝ_0^ΠΓ^! → Z = M[0], defined by (51), (52). Restrict it to the subgroups Z^{!'}, Z^{!'''}, Z^{!0}, of indices 2, 2, 4 in Z^!.
- On each of these, A is multiplicative, i.e. a homomorphism.
- Its images are the subgroups Ŝ_0^{Π_0}Γ^{!'}, Ŝ_0^{Π_0}Γ^{!'''}, Ŝ_0^{Π_0}Γ^{!0}, of indices 4, 4, 8.
- These images split the inverse images, giving (83): Ŝ_0^ΠΓ^{!*} = Ŝ_0^{Π_0}Γ^{!*} × μ.
- (a) The first two are not normal. (b) The third is normal.

Consequence. The extension Ŝ_0^ΠΓ^! of Z^! by μ is canonically the pullback, along Z^! → Z^!/Z^{!0} ≅ μ×μ (via (ε_3, ε_2)), of the order-8 central extension E = Ŝ_0^ΠΓ^!/Ŝ_0^{Π_0}Γ^{!0} of μ×μ by μ.

Next page. Grothendieck identifies E: are all its elements of order ≤ 2? He also uses E, through covariant/contravariant functoriality of Ext and the diagonal μ → L_ρ×L_σ, to recover the extension of Z^! by L_ρ×L_σ.

Margin. He asks whether there is a section of the whole extension Ŝ_0^ΠΓ of Ẑ by μ, described as 'algebraic' or automorphic, that agrees with A on Ẑ^{!'} and Ẑ^{!'''}.

Purpose. To pin down the ±1 (SL_2 over PSL_2-type) central extension that sits over the genus-0 modular/Teichmüller group in his Galois–Teichmüller ('lacets') framework. Concretely, he reduces it to a finite cohomology class in H^2(μ×μ, μ).
errors: Equation number (82) is used twice: once for the exact sequence on page 598 and again for the product decomposition here.
Calling the extension 'centrale' adds nothing: any extension by μ = Z/2 is automatically central, since Aut(Z/2) = 1. Not a mathematical error.

Index bookkeeping is consistent: Z^{!0} has index 4 in Z^! and the kernel μ has order 2, giving index 8; Z^{!'} and Z^{!'''} have index 2, giving 4. A normal complement to μ inside the inverse image of Z^{!0} does force the extension to be pulled back from Z^!/Z^{!0}. No gap is visible on this page beyond reliance on the earlier computations (76)–(80).

ideas.what: Splitting of the μ-extension over finite-index subgroups via a canonical section that is multiplicative there.
ideas.modern_name: Restriction of a 2-cocycle class to subgroups on which it vanishes; explicit splittings

ideas.what: Normality test for the three splitting subgroups: two are not normal, the index-8 one is normal. Hence the extension is inflated from an order-8 central extension of μ×μ by μ.
ideas.modern_name: Inflation from a finite quotient; class in H^2(Z/2×Z/2, Z/2)

ideas.what: Studying the ±1 central extension (SL_2 over PSL_2-type, with ρ^3 = σ^2 = −1) over the genus-0 modular/Teichmüller group inside a Galois–Teichmüller group of triples (u,a,b), using characters ε_2, ε_3.
ideas.modern_name: Lifting GT/Galois actions from PSL_2-type to SL_2-type profinite groups; central extensions of the profinite modular group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (GT, 1990); Ihara; Lochak–Schneps; Nakamura (1990s) for related lifting questions
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche (1981) sketches the Teichmüller tower and Galois action but not these computations

missed.claim: The margin asks whether the μ-extension of the full Ẑ admits a global section (described as algebraic or automorphic) that restricts to the canonical section A on the two non-normal index-2 pieces. The page does not answer this.
missed.quote: La question se pose s'il existe une section ... de l'ext. Ŝ_0^ΠΓ de Ẑ par μ, qui soit ... A sur Ẑ^{!'''}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a concrete compatibility question for the ±1-lift of Galois–Teichmüller actions to SL_2-type groups. That theme recurs in work on GT and the profinite SL_2(Z), but probably not in this precise form.

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but routine group-theoretic bookkeeping (splittings, normality, inflation from an order-8 group) inside Grothendieck's private GT-type framework. The only open item is a marginal question about a compatible section; nothing seems to be a substantive unknown result.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 likely reads '[l'extension] se scinde conséquemment par Ŝ_0^{Π_0}Γ^{!0}' (or similar), not 'se-dit'. The 'Γ_0' there should be Γ^{!0}.
'qui est multiplication par ces sous-groupes' should read 'qui est multiplicative sur ces sous-groupes'.

The final sentence reads roughly 'est canoniquement l'image inverse d'une extension centrale bien définie (Ŝ_0^ΠΓ^!/Ŝ_0^{Π_0}Γ^{!0}) de Z^!/Z^{!0} ≃ μ×μ par μ'. The struck-through word is 'par', not 'pour'.
The insertion above 'restrictions par' is uncertain ('transportées' or 'transversales').
The margin likely ends '...qui soit A sur Ẑ^{!'} et sur Ẑ^{!'''}'. The '(Algébrique)' reading is uncertain.
